title: P0: Hosted API duplicate-hedge fallout — incident review & runbook draft
content:
Summary

At ~2029-11-21T09:18:00Z we observed a P0 impact affecting Hosted API streaming and non-streaming paths: a sustained p95/p99 latency surge, elevated 5xx rate (mainly 503/504), and intermittent stream handshake failures. The degradation lasted ~42 minutes; mitigations were applied and the system returned to baseline after 09:57Z.

High-level hypothesis

A recently rolled hedging/config feature caused duplicate hedged requests to be sent to upstream inference backends under certain latency threshold conditions. The duplicate fanout amplified load on the KV cache and the edge acceptor layer, causing connection queueing and ephemeral port exhaustion on the edge proxies. That cascade led to timeouts and 5xx from the edge->backend path and caused many streaming sessions to fail during early handshake frames.

Why this is unique/different from previous incidents

- Root cue is not purely autoscaler or memory pressure; it's a request-fanout amplification introduced by a hedging config change rolled without a canary gating on streaming-heavy prefixes.
- The incident manifested primarily as handshake + acceptor saturation rather than slow model inference times.

Timeline (UTC, rough)

- 09:15:30 — Canary rollout of edge hedging feature flag started (edge-config PR #412). 10% of edges targeted via config service.
- 09:17:40 — Datadog alert: hostedapi.p99_latency > baseline by +180% (global).
- 09:18:03 — First spike in upstream request_count per-second per-edge; non-streaming generation requests doubled on affected edges.
- 09:19:10 — Error budget alert: hostedapi.5xx_rate > 1% for 3m; paging triggered (SRE oncall: Liam).
- 09:20:00 — Observed increasing ephemeral socket ESTABLISHED counts and acceptor backlog growth on edge hosts (telemetry from edge-acceptor).
- 09:23:40 — SRE runbook step: flip hedging flag -> set rollout back to 0% in config service (command noted below). Initial results ambiguous because cached config persisted on some proxies.
- 09:29:00 — Upstream retries/duplicate request metrics still elevated (cache invalidation lag); applied emergency edge-level client throttling (edge-rate-limit profile) at 09:31.
- 09:38:00 — Acceptable decline in connection backlog on majority of edges; streaming handshake success ratio improving.
- 09:45:00 — All affected edges reporting normal p95/p99; 5xx rate returned to baseline by 09:57:00.

Impact

- Duration: ~42 minutes of elevated latency and 5xx for ~20% of production traffic.
- User-visible: slow responses and intermittent failures for streaming sessions for some customers (largest impact for customers with many short-turn streaming sessions).
- Billing/financial: small, transient error budget consumption; no immediate financial exposure identified.

Telemetry/signals observed

- request_fanout_multiplier metric spiked from 1.0 -> 1.9 on affected edges shortly after 09:18Z.
- upstream_request_rate increased proportionally, but model_inference_time stayed within normal bounds -> suggests amplification at edge, not backend slowdown.
- edge_acceptor_backlog_size per host increased 2–4x above normal.
- ephemeral_port_usage on edge proxies increased; some hosts hit 80–92% of ephemeral socket table limits.
- stream_handshake_success_rate dropped ~25% on affected edges.
- traces show duplicate hedged requests with near-identical trace ids and different upstream target shards.

Immediate mitigation steps (what we executed)

1) Rollback hedging rollout in config service (09:23). Command (internal): curl -X POST https://config-service.internal/flags/hedging/rollout -d '{"percent":0}'
2) Apply immediate edge-level rate limit profile to degrade non-critical short-stream paths (09:31). k8s job to patch Envoy config via rollout: kubectl patch -n edge deploy/edge-proxy --patch '{...}' (see playbook run log).
3) Scale up edge acceptor pool by increasing acceptor replicas by +20% as an emergency (09:27) — mitigated hosts nearing ephemeral limits.
4) Invalidate config cache on long-tailed edges via remote restart where cache TTL prevented config flip (09:33–09:40).

Why rollback alone didn't immediately fix it

- Config cache TTLs and some legacy proxies read config from a local snapshot; a subset of hosts retained hedging behavior until cache expiry or restart.
- Hedging amplified requests into backends and stressed caches; even after rollback started, the elevated fanout and acceptor backlog persisted until hosts cycled or rate limits applied.

Root cause analysis (evidence + hypothesis)

- Code change: hedging logic added a duplication path for requests when observed latency exceeded a dynamic threshold. The threshold calculation had an off-by-one bug in percentiles (used p99 instead of p95 baseline) which made the hedger more aggressive for edges with high variance.
- The config rollout targeted streaming prefixes indirectly (via prefix regex) and unintentionally included many short-lived streaming sessions which are sensitive to even small extra latency and duplicate requests.
- The duplicate requests were directed to different backend shards (intended), which multiplied KV cache pressure and increased connection churn.
- Telemetry and traces: confirmed duplicate request ids with same client id and two outgoing requests within 30–120ms window. No backend inference errors to explain delay — amplification purely front-end.

Contributing factors

- No canary policy for streaming-heavy prefixes in the rollout plan.
- Config cache TTLs too long for emergency rollbacks (up to 10 minutes on some proxies).
- Lack of a test harness that simulates hedging with short-stream session patterns.
- Missing alerting for sudden increases in duplicate_request_ratio (we had the metric but no page threshold).

Runbook draft (short play steps for oncall)

- Detect: alert hostedapi.duplicate_request_ratio > 0.5 for 1m OR edge_acceptor_backlog_size > critical threshold.
- First actions: set hedging flag rollout to 0% (config service) -> confirm via /flags API on edge hosts.
- If duplicates persist > 2m: enforce edge rate-limits on streaming_short namespace and patch Envoy to reject overtly duplicated connections (see emergency Envoy config snippet).
- If acceptor backlog increasing: scale acceptor replicas, and increase socket table ephemeral range on edge hosts as temporary patch.
- If 5xx persisted after rollback > 5m: perform host-level restart of edge proxies in a rolling manner limited to 5% at a time.
- Communication: update #sre-incident-3217 Slack channel and the incident doc every 10 minutes while active.

Command cheatsheet (for responders)

- Check duplicate metric: datadog query hostedapi.duplicate_request_ratio{env:prod}.rollup(avg,60)
- Flip rollout: curl -X POST https://config-service.internal/flags/hedging/rollout -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"percent":0}'
- Force config reload on edge host (where safe): ssh edge-N && sudo systemctl restart edge-proxy
- Patch envoy rate limit (example): kubectl -n edge patch envoyconfig hedging-ratelimit --type merge --patch '{"spec":{"limits":{"short_stream":200}}}'

Longer-term fixes / action items (owner / due)

- SRE-3218: Implement canary gating by traffic profile (disallow hedging on streaming-heavy prefixes) — Owner: Liam Chen — Due: 2029-12-05.
- SRE-3219: Shorten config cache TTL for edge proxies and add a fast-invalidating emergency path — Owner: Noah Rivera — Due: 2029-12-01.
- SRE-3220: Add duplicate_request_ratio to paging alerts and dashboards; add a runbook for hedging anomalies — Owner: Asha Patel — Due: 2029-11-30.
- SRE-3221: Create a test harness that replays short-stream session patterns against hedging logic before rollout — Owner: Evelyn Park — Due: 2029-12-15.
- ENG-4207: Fix hedging percentile bug (p99/p95 mismatch) and add unit/integration tests — Owner: Platform Serving Team (PR #412 follow-up) — Due: 2029-11-29.

Post-incident notes / unresolved questions

- Why did some edge hosts not pick up config update after rollback? Investigate config service agent logs for cache invalidation failures (ticketed SRE-3222).
- Need a better way to tag traffic profiles so rollout targeting can exclude streaming-short prefixes. Work with Product to define prefix tagging semantics.
- Confirm whether any client SDKs retried aggressively on observed 503s and contributed to fanout; correlate client-side telemetry for top impacted customers.

Communication log (brief)

- 09:20 — Page sent to SRE; initial post to #sre-incident-3217 with context.
- 09:25 — Edge-config rollback called and noted in Slack.
- 09:31 — Edge rate-limits applied; update posted.
- 09:58 — Incident declared resolved; post-incident channel maintained for follow-ups.

Lessons learned (TL;DR)

- New request-level features that duplicate/fanout must have explicit negative-targeting for streaming-short patterns and must be canaried by traffic profile, not just by % of hosts.
- Config cache invalidation and emergency rollback semantics are critical — reduce TTLs and/or implement forced invalidation RPC.
- Instrument duplicate_request_ratio and make it a first-class paging signal.

Appendix: quick links and artifacts

- Runtime traces (sample): https://trace.redwood.internal/trace/abc123 (anonymized example)
- Datadog dashboard (hedging): https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/hedging-3217
- PR that rolled the config: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-config/pull/412
- Incident timeline sheet: Confluence: SRE-3217 timeline (link above)

Draft status & next steps

This doc is a working draft for the post-incident review. Please add notes/corrections inline. Next sync: quick SRE postmortem review on 2029-11-24 16:00 UTC (30m).

Open action owners: see 'Longer-term fixes' above. Mark items done in JIRA and reference this incident ID (SRE-3217) when closing.
